(b) 'above the minimum, sorted': the filtering and the ordering are the server's (closed decisions 'Minimum co-changes' and 'Sort order' live in `coupling.ts`), so what this task owed was to draw what arrives without re-sorting and without re-deriving the threshold — it maps in arrival order and reads `coupling.minCoOccurrences` off the payload. Both tests the **TDD:** line names are in the diff, and each body matches its sentence. `test('draws a row per coupled pair with its percent')` (web/src/Heat.test.tsx:254) sends two pairs through `stubHeat(TREE, pairs)` and asserts `screen.getAllByTestId('coupling-row')` has length 2 and that their `textContent` equals `['checkout ↔ ui · 80%', 'checkout ↔ pago.ts · 40%']` — same testid, both percents, in the order the double sent them, which is exactly the plan's 'in the order the double sent them'. `test('a level with no pair above the minimum says so instead of an empty list')` (web/src/Heat.test.tsx:273) sends `pairs: []` and asserts `findByText('Ninguna pareja llega a 5 cambios juntos en esta ventana')` plus `queryAllByTestId('coupling-row')` empty; that literal is what `noCouplingHeadline(5)` returns in web/src/format.ts:144-146, so the plan's `noCouplingHeadline(5)` is pinned by its literal text rather than by re-calling the production function — same assertion, same input, same expected value.

No `Contract (path):` block in this task. The `Current state (web/src/Heat.tsx, lines 206-211)` block is honoured: the heat footer div and the `</>`/`)}` closing survive untouched and the new section is inserted between them. The `Call site (web/src/Heat.tsx)` block is reproduced name by name — same guards (`coupling !== null && couplingRows(coupling.pairs).length === 0`), same key (`${row.a}|${row.b}`), same testid, same row text `{row.a} ↔ {row.b} · {row.percent}%` — and the imports the brief names arrive from the modules it names (`couplingRows` from `./heat-rows`, `noCouplingHeadline`/`couplingFooter` from `./format`). The one addition to the Call site text is `style={ROW_STYLE}` on the row div; the block is not a `Final text` block, and `ROW_STYLE` is the constant the existing heat rows already use (web/src/Heat.tsx:265), so this is the host file's own idiom, not a different contract.

Three rows bear on this diff and each is implemented with the value it states. 'Row cap in the UI: COUPLING_ROW_LIMIT = 8, its own constant in web/src/heat-rows.ts' — the component draws through `couplingRows`, which slices at that constant (heat-rows.ts:74-75); no second cap in Heat.tsx. 'MIN_CO_OCCURRENCES = 5 ... echoed in the payload as minCoOccurrences so the UI can say why a pair does not show' — the empty state and the footer both read `coupling.minCoOccurrences` and neither hard-codes 5 in production code. 'Sort order: percent descending, ties by coChanges, then a' — a server-side decision; the block does not re-order what it receives, which is what leaves that row the only place the order is decided. The remaining rows (percent formula, scope of a pair, the new endpoint, the shape of the server module, where the child/main-folder decisions live) are server-side and this diff leaves them alone.

Exemplars: the new section imitates `web/src/Heat.tsx`'s own idiom (the block extended in place, per §3) — the `role="alert"` error paragraph mirrors the existing `{error !== null &&

...}` at Heat.tsx:129, the footer div copies the heat footer's style object verbatim, and the row reuses `ROW_STYLE`. In the tests, `stubHeat` is extended exactly as §3 asks ('the fetch double this slice extends to also answer the coupling endpoint') and it answers **by URL**, via `isCouplingRequest(url)`, not by call order — which is both §3's rule and `conventions/testing.md`'s 'A double of a whole conversation answers by what it is asked, not by order'. AGENTS.md: identifiers, helper names, comments and test names are English (`couplingOf`, `couplingFor`, `isCouplingRequest`, 'draws a row per coupled pair with its percent'); the UI copy stays Spanish ('Acoplamiento', `noCouplingHeadline`), which is what that rule reserves for product vocabulary. No relative import in `web/` gained a `.js` suffix and nothing in `web/` imports from `server/` (the `Coupling`/`CouplingPair` types come from `./api/types`). No author name or email anywhere. `conventions/style.md`: all three files are `(modify)` of modules that pre-date the document, so the declared-debt exemption covers their JSDoc comments and their module-level test helpers; the diff adds nothing that is a new concept smuggled into an old file — the new coupling module was born in Task 2, and here the section, the row helper and the double extension genuinely extend what was already in these files. `conventions/decisions.md`: the minimum is not written a second time in the UI (it is read off the payload) and the row cap is not re-derived; the child/main-folder decisions are untouched. `conventions/simplicity.md`: no new export, no new parameter without a caller, no guard downstream of a door. `couplingRows(coupling.pairs)` is called twice (once for the length test, once for the map) — that is the shape the brief's own Call site block prescribes, so it is not this item's finding. `CouplingRow.barWidth` stays unread by the new row, but that field arrived in an earlier task's `heat-rows.ts` and this diff does not touch that file. `conventions/boundaries.md` and `conventions/domain.md`: nothing in this diff crosses the outer edge or names a domain word — the payload types and the client already existed. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — no subject added by this diff; the classifiers it renders (`aKind`/`bKind`: `'dir' | 'file'`, api/types.ts:109-116) are already a closed vocabulary and the diff neither collapses them into a boolean nor dispatches over them with a catch-all. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: `couplingOf` and `couplingFor` return declared `Coupling` objects, and the component consumes `Coupling`/`CouplingRow` fields, never a map by key lookup. (3) two fields that have to agree, sentinel for an absence — no subject added: the absence of a loaded payload is carried by `Coupling | null`, the empty state is *derived* from `couplingRows(...).length === 0` rather than from a flag, and no empty string or zero stands in for 'none' (the pre-existing `coupling`/`couplingError` state pair comes from Task 7's effect, which this diff does not touch). (4) an error named for where it happens — no subject: this diff declares no error type; it renders the existing `ApiErrorCode`, whose members name what happened (`git-failed`, `invalid-body`). No clash between a control of the plan and any of these documents.

There are `-` lines in both test files, and I read every one against the brief: none leaves a pre-existing test asserting less. In web/src/Heat.test.tsx the removals are (a) the helper rename `emptyCouplingOf(level)` -> `couplingOf(level, pairs)` with `pairs: []` becoming `pairs: [...pairs]`, (b) `stubHeat`'s signature gaining `pairs: readonly CouplingPair[] = []`, and (c) three inline doubles (`stubServer`, the fallback test, the rejected-save test) changing `okResponse(level)` into `okResponse(isCouplingRequest(url) ? couplingOf(level, []) : level)`. The default `[]` makes every pre-existing call site of `stubHeat` answer exactly what it answered before, the non-coupling branch of the three inline doubles returns the identical body, and not one `expect` in the file is removed, relaxed or rewritten — the rejected-save test still pins `urls.slice(asked)` to `['/api/repos/alpha/settings']`, the fallback test still pins both halves of its notice, and `stubServer`'s test still pins the same percentages, footers and option lists. What those three changes buy is a *valid* `Coupling` for the `/coupling` request they previously answered with a `Heat` body, which is the arrange this task's rendering needs; before it, `coupling.pairs` would have been `undefined`. In web/src/App.test.tsx the only `-` lines are the type import and the last arm of the body ternary, both replaced by the added `url.includes('/coupling?') ? couplingFor(url) :` branch — the plan states this in words ('No assertion in `App.test.tsx` changes'), and the diff bears that out.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by the scaffolding. Splitting the diff: web/src/Heat.tsx is production; web/src/Heat.test.tsx and web/src/App.test.tsx are the tests' own doubles. The rows, their text and the empty-state sentence come from Heat.tsx:241-258 together with `couplingRows` (web/src/heat-rows.ts:74) and `noCouplingHeadline`/`couplingFooter` (web/src/format.ts:144-151) — all production modules. The test contributes only the payload the fetch double answers with (`couplingOf`), and its expected values are the rendered strings, not values the test computed: revert the Heat.tsx block and `getAllByTestId('coupling-row')` returns nothing and `findByText('Ninguna pareja llega a 5 cambios juntos en esta ventana')` times out. No hard-coded expected value stands in for a missing production line.

`### Out of scope` names coupling across repos, complexity hotspots, coupling over time, changing anything of Pulso or Gente, and a navigation other than Calor's: the diff touches none of them — it adds no state, no route, no navigation, and its only component change is inside the existing `HeatBlock` render. Inside the declared files every line traces to a sentence of the task. Heat.tsx: the section the `Call site` block prescribes. Heat.test.tsx: the two tests **Tests:** lists, plus the `stubHeat` extension §3 asks for; the `emptyCouplingOf` -> `couplingOf(level, pairs)` rename is that extension seen from the helper — the task needs a double that can send two pairs, and the same helper reused by the three inline doubles is what keeps a single wording of the coupling payload in this file (`conventions/decisions.md`), so it is not a refactor the task did not ask for. App.test.tsx: the committed plan's Task 8 section carries this file in its `**Files:**` line (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-issue-51-acoplamiento-temporal.md:631-632) and spells out the change in prose at lines 634-641 — a `'/coupling?'` branch answering a minimal empty `Coupling` — which is exactly and only what the diff writes there.

Two new tests, both with the three properties. Deterministic: neither reads the clock, the network or the filesystem — `fetch` is doubled with `vi.stubGlobal` and every value is a literal in the file; no randomness, no sleep (they synchronise with `waitFor`/`findByText`, which is the awaited condition, not a delay). Isolated: each builds its own state through `stubHeat(TREE, ...)` and `render(...)`, the stub is undone by the setup file's `vi.unstubAllGlobals()`, and neither depends on an order — `TREE` is read, never mutated, and the second test passes `[]` explicitly instead of leaning on the default. Verifies real behaviour: both assert on rendered DOM produced by Heat.tsx — the row `textContent` `['checkout ↔ ui · 80%', 'checkout ↔ pago.ts · 40%']` and the literal empty-state sentence — not on a call count, a stub's return value or a constant the test defined; with the production lines of this diff reverted both fail. Nothing to report as `high`. The finer half could not be measured with the text the implementer was given: the skill `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` failed to load ('Unknown skill'), so per this item I report only the three properties above and no preference of my own. Read against `conventions/testing.md`, which did arrive: each test name is the sentence and says what is guaranteed, and each assertion could fail for the reason its name gives — the row test on the literal row text (not a loose substring), the empty-state test on the whole distinctive sentence plus the absence of any row.
